lessons.title: Security Control Categories
lessons.introduction: Security controls can be grouped by how they are implemented: technical, managerial, operational, and physical.
lessons.whyItMatters: MSPs use tools, governance, technician procedures and building protections together. Category identifies the primary implementation mechanism.

steps.title: Two independent questions
steps.content: Ask: what category is the control, and what type is it? Category describes implementation. Type describes intended effect.

checkpoint.prompt: Is preventive a category or a type?
checkpoint.feedback: Preventive describes purpose, not implementation category.

steps.title: Technical
steps.content: Technical controls are enforced primarily by hardware, software, firmware or configuration.

example.scenario: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access blocks unmanaged devices.

checkpoint.prompt: An Intune compliance policy blocks an unmanaged device. Category?

steps.title: Managerial
steps.content: Managerial controls establish governance, risk decisions, policies, standards and oversight.

example.scenario: Leadership approves a risk treatment plan and acceptable-use policy.

checkpoint.prompt: A board-approved risk policy is which category?

steps.title: Operational
steps.content: Operational controls are performed mainly by people following repeatable procedures.

example.scenario: A technician follows the leaver checklist and disables accounts.

checkpoint.prompt: A technician follows an incident runbook. Category?
checkpoint.feedback: The control is executed through a human process.

steps.title: Physical
steps.content: Physical controls protect people, facilities, equipment and physical access.

example.scenario: A badge-controlled comms-room door and CCTV protect network hardware.

checkpoint.prompt: A locked server-cabinet door is which category?

steps.title: Category recap
steps.content: Classify by the primary mechanism: technology, governance, human procedure or physical barrier.

checkpoint.prompt: A policy plus an automated block are one category?
checkpoint.feedback: The policy is managerial; automated enforcement is technical.

lessons.title: Security Control Types
lessons.introduction: Control type describes the control's primary intended effect.
lessons.whyItMatters: Exam scenarios often include controls with several effects. Select the type matching the scenario's stated primary purpose and timing.

steps.title: Purpose and timing
steps.content: Ask whether the control stops, discourages, discovers, restores, substitutes or instructs.
steps.memoryCue: Stop, scare, spot, restore, substitute, instruct.

checkpoint.prompt: Does type describe implementation or purpose?

steps.title: Preventive
steps.content: Preventive controls block or reduce the likelihood of an unwanted event.

example.scenario: A Conditional Access rule blocks legacy authentication.

checkpoint.prompt: A firewall deny rule is primarily what type?
checkpoint.feedback: It blocks traffic before access occurs.

steps.title: Deterrent
steps.content: Deterrent controls discourage behaviour by increasing perceived risk or consequences.

example.scenario: Visible CCTV signs discourage unauthorised entry.

checkpoint.prompt: A warning banner is primarily what type?

steps.title: Detective
steps.content: Detective controls identify or alert on events that occurred or are occurring.

example.scenario: Microsoft Sentinel raises an impossible-travel alert.

checkpoint.prompt: A SIEM alert is primarily what type?

steps.title: Corrective
steps.content: Corrective controls repair damage, remove effects or restore normal operation after an event.

example.scenario: A technician restores a server from a clean backup.

checkpoint.prompt: Restoring from backup is what type?

steps.title: Compensating
steps.content: Compensating controls provide an alternative when the preferred control is unavailable or impractical, while addressing the same intent.

example.scenario: A restricted jump host is used because a legacy platform cannot support MFA.

checkpoint.feedback: It must substitute for an unavailable or impractical preferred control.

steps.title: Directive
steps.content: Directive controls instruct or require people to act in a specified way.

example.scenario: An acceptable-use policy requires staff to report suspected phishing.

checkpoint.prompt: A mandatory security policy is primarily what type?

steps.title: Type recap
steps.content: Choose the primary purpose named by the scenario, then classify category separately.
steps.memoryCue: Stop, discourage, discover, restore, substitute, instruct.

checkpoint.prompt: Can a technical control also be detective?
checkpoint.feedback: Category and type are separate axes.
